subject: technology
topic: Algorithmic curation is narrowing your exposure to divergent viewpoints
angle: While some research shows algorithms amplify ideological homogeneity, other studies find that personalization does not necessarily reduce news diversity and can even match human editors in variety.
title: The Architecture of Your Feed

hooks.text: Is your feed actually showing you everything?
You assume algorithms isolate you, but they can also match human editors.
You are consuming a select set of content chosen for you.
A screen glows in a dark room.

reveal.headline: Algorithmic systems structurally amplify ideological homogeneity.
reveal.body: While some studies show personalization can match human editorial variety, internet customization effectively isolates individuals from diverse opinions.

explain.headline: The evidence on your news feed is mixed.
explain.body: Some research shows personalization does not reduce news diversity. Other studies show systems reinforce selective exposure and limit your viewpoint diversity.

matters.headline: Your information diet is shaped by invisible logic.
matters.body: That may be why you see a select set of content. The systems are designed to reinforce what you already see.

example.headline: You scroll through your feed on a quiet evening.
example.body: The headlines match your previous interests. The stories feel familiar. You do not see the news from the other side of the street.

question.headline: Who is choosing what you see?
question.body: You are only seeing a select set.

verdict: The evidence is mixed, with some studies confirming the existence of filter bubbles and others finding that the effects on news diversity may be exaggerated or manageable.
caveat: The evidence base suffers from geographic bias toward Western contexts, limited longitudinal research, and methodological fragmentation.
caption:
Algorithmic curation determines the boundaries of your information world.

Research shows mixed results: some studies find personalization maintains news diversity, while others prove systems structurally amplify ideological homogeneity. The evidence is limited by geographic bias and a lack of longitudinal data.

What part of your feed feels most curated?
